scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Uniform Matrix Hitting Points in Every Positive Characteristic” (preprints/Uniform-Matrix-Hitting-Points-in-Every-Positive-Characteristic-October-4-2026/uniform-matrix-hitting-points-positive-characteristic.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 116 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 06284554d3db1df4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 1-2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a deterministic Turing machine and absolute positive integers C, k with the following property. Given a prime p in binary and positive integers n, s in unary, the machine outputs a positive integer d = O(n3s6) and a tuple (T1, . . . , Tn) ∈ Matd(Fp)n . For every field F of characteristic p and every nonzero f ∈ F⟨x1, . . . , xn⟩ computed by a formula of size at most s, the same tuple, viewed over F, satisfies f(T1, . . . , Tn) ̸= 0. 1 Writing L = ⌈log2 p⌉, the total running time and output length are at most C(n + s + L + 1)k. All matrix entries are output densely as ordinary binary residues in {0, . . . , p − 1}, with dimensions and separators included. Primality of p is promised.
